title: Transpilation and Qubit Connectivity
summary: Basis gates, coupling maps, SWAP insertion, and why the number of two-qubit gates is the cost of a circuit on hardware.
objectives: Transpile a circuit to a basis-gate set and a coupling map with qiskit.transpile
Explain why a two-qubit gate between non-neighbors costs extra two-qubit gates
Measure the cost of a transpiled circuit with count_ops() and depth()
Reduce the cost by writing a logical circuit that matches the device connectivity
mission: A device has 4 qubits in a line (0 - 1 - 2 - 3) and runs only rz, sx, x and cx. Prepare the GHZ state (|0000⟩ + |1111⟩)/√2 and store in qc the transpiled circuit, with at most 3 two-qubit gates. Every cx in qc must act on neighboring qubits.

prediction.question: On a line 0 - 1 - 2, with logical qubits 0, 1, 2 placed on the physical qubits 0, 1, 2, a circuit contains one cx(0, 2). How many cx gates does the transpiled circuit contain?
options: 1: the gate is already a CNOT
3: one SWAP makes the qubits neighbors
4: one SWAP (3 cx) plus the cx itself
prediction.explanation: Qubits 0 and 2 are not neighbors, so the transpiler moves one of them next to the other with a SWAP. A SWAP is 3 CNOTs, and the original CNOT still has to run. Total: 3 + 1 = 4.

hints: Run the starter code and read count_ops(): the star-shaped circuit (every cx starts at qubit 0) needs SWAPs on a line, so it ends with 6 cx. Each SWAP is 3 cx.
Transpilation does not change the algorithm, it only maps it to the device. The cost depends on the circuit you give it. Write a GHZ circuit in which every cx acts on a pair of neighbors of the line.
Apply h(0), then a chain of CNOTs: ghz.cx(0, 1), ghz.cx(1, 2), ghz.cx(2, 3). Transpile ghz into qc with the same coupling_map and basis_gates: three cx and no SWAP.

messages.ok: The circuit uses only rz, sx, x and cx, every cx acts on neighbors, it prepares the GHZ state, and it has {count} two-qubit gates (depth {depth}).
messages.no_circuit: Store the transpiled circuit in the variable qc.
messages.wrong_qubits: The device has 4 qubits, but qc has {count}.
messages.not_basis: qc contains gates outside the basis: {gates}. Pass basis_gates to transpile.
messages.not_adjacent: A two-qubit gate acts on qubits {a} and {b}, which are not neighbors in the line 0 - 1 - 2 - 3. Pass coupling_map to transpile.
messages.not_unitary: qc contains measurements or other non-unitary operations. Keep only the gates that prepare the state.
messages.wrong_state: qc does not prepare the GHZ state: the fidelity with (|0000⟩ + |1111⟩)/√2 is {fidelity}.
messages.too_many: qc has {count} two-qubit gates, but the budget is {budget}. Change the circuit you transpile so that fewer SWAPs are needed.
